To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

relativistic kinematics is essential in electron-deuteron calculations and that the effects of negative energies and meson retardations are small in the kinematic region that is currently being studied at Jefferson Lab.

the relativistic corrections to the deuteron electromagnetic form factors are negligible for the kinematics of interest, and that the meson-exchange corrections are large and positive for the electric form factor and negative for the magnetic form factor.

relativistic corrections in electron-deuteron elastic scattering are small in the kinematic region that is probed at Jefferson Lab, and the inclusion of the {rho}{gamma}{pi} meson-exchage current in electron-deutreon elastic scattering does not significantly change the results of the calculation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of relativistic methods for the study of nuclear structure.
the development of a relativistic theory for the description of two-body bound states.
the application of a relativistic three-dimensional formalism to the problem of calculating two-body bound-state observables in a realistic model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this relativistic approach is a very useful tool to calculate the electromagnetic structure of the deuteron and to compare with the experimental results.
the relativistic three-dimensional formalism provides a consistent and complete theoretical framework for the study of two-body systems.
relativistic effects do not appear to have any significant effect on the observables of interest.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the relativistic three-dimensional theory of two-body bound states provides a systematic framework to include relativistic kinematics in calculations of electron scattering from two-body bound states.
the three-dimensional formalism is a viable approach for studying electron scattering from two-body bound states.
the three-body Faddeev calculations of electron-deuteron elastic scattering are in excellent agreement with the experimental data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the meson-exchange currents have a significant impact on the calculated cross sections and the extracted form factors.
the meson-exchange contribution to A, B, T{sub 10}, and T{sub {Delta}} is small, and the meson-exchanges do not have a large effect on the shape of the cross sections.
the meson-exchange currents are very important for understanding electron-deuteron data.
